LHX.sentence: L3Harris has lagged its bigger defense rivals lately and its profit margins are running thinner than usual, but military demand hasn't changed, so this looks like a cheap moment for the smallest of the defense primes.

ASML.sentence: ASML is sitting right near its all-time high and just drifting quietly — as the only company on earth making a certain kind of chipmaking machine, that's exactly where you'd expect it to be.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet, slightly-down week — selling oxygen and nitrogen under long contracts is a steady business, and there's not much of a story right now.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quietly outrunning its peers as the AI-cloud story keeps grinding along, no drama attached.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is flat, but biotech funding is thawing again, and since that money eventually turns into orders for their lab equipment, it's a quietly encouraging sign a few quarters out.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge dipped a little, but this pipeline toll-collector is paying a generous dividend that's now near the high end of its usual range, which makes it look reasonably cheap.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen a lot from its high — steeper than you'd expect for a company whose corporate and government customers keep signing multi-year contracts for its workflow and AI tools — so the drop looks more like nerves than a real problem.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore ticked up nicely and is paying a hefty dividend backed by its huge commodity-trading arm, so it's a steady stretch for the miner-and-trader.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta slipped a touch, but the headline price of its rock looks weak only because of how the mix is counted — strip that out and the real price per ton is still rising, which is the part that matters for this quarry business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA had a good day, helped by a strong Mexican peso — since most of this Latin American Coke bottler's sales are in pesos, a firmer currency lifts what those sales are worth to us.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras had a rough day, down about 4%, but oil prices are healthy and this Brazilian oil giant is paying one of the biggest dividends around right now.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk pulled back after a big run-up — a spike in shipping rates had pushed the stock up sharply, and it's now cooling off from those stretched levels.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is flat, but oddly it's trading at a slight discount to Visa even though it's the faster-growing of the two payment networks — a rare mispricing given people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker slipped while other medical-device stocks rallied, which looks more like investors souring on the group's leader than anything actually wrong with the business.
